# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old  <sub>[v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c28 P2](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v2 c28 P27](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has an exceptionally beautiful, delicate face with chestnut curls that he later wears short, a crimson mouth, and dark blue eyes that match his father's. He is small for his age at ten, but eventually grows very tall by sixteen.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P28](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0028), [v2 c23 P23](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0023), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)_

## Personality

Paul is a meditative, highly imaginative, and sensitive boy with a deep capacity for poetic thought and imagery. Though dreamy and introspective, he possesses a manly, courageous nature and holds his own in school yard games. He is deeply loyal to those he loves, polite, and very fair-minded in his judgments.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020)_

## History

Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea to live with his grandmother and attends Avonlea school, quickly bonding with his new teacher, Anne Shirley, over their shared imaginative nature. He shares his inner world of 'rock people' with Anne, who becomes his mentor and closest friend. He later introduces Anne to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, unwittingly helping to set in motion the reunion and marriage of Miss Lavendar and his father, Stephen Irving. Following his father's remarriage, Paul happily accepts Miss Lavendar as his 'Mother Lavendar' and spends his summers with them at Echo Lodge. As he grows older, Paul begins writing poetry, developing his literary talent. After completing his schooling at Avonlea, he goes abroad for two years of study.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c5 P22](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0022), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c28 P27](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0027), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030), [v4 c17 P26](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0026)_

## Background by volume

- Raised in the United States by his father after his mother died when he was seven  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004)</sub>
- Sent to Avonlea to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047)</sub>
- Created an elaborate world of imaginary 'rock people' on the shore  <sub>[v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041)</sub>

## Quotes

> I think an angel walks over the world after the sun sets... a great, tall, white angel, with silvery folded wings... and sings the flowers and birds to sleep. Children can hear him if they know how to listen.  <sub>[v2 c19 P28](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0028)</sub>

> I think the violets are little snips of the sky that fell down when the angels cut out holes for the stars to shine through. And the buttercups are made out of old sunshine; and I think the sweet peas will be butterflies when they go to heaven.  <sub>[v2 c19 P32](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0032)</sub>

> Isn't it splendid to be that kind, teacher?  <sub>[v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019)</sub>

> It's a fine thing to have a father you can depend on, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c29 P2](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0002)</sub>

> To me you'll always be 'Teacher'—the teacher of the best lessons I ever learned.  <sub>[v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)</sub>
